finding: No typed channel for 'open, awaiting your decision — do not re-raise'. alreadyBuilt's awaiting-owner case assumes the fix is BUILT, so an undecided item had no slot and correctness fell back to prose the scout may not honour.
evidence: The Manager hand-wrote 'don't dispatch, don't re-raise as new' for W3. Same class as the 24 declines that existed only as prose.
note: Shipped as the openKnown arg, distinct from alreadyBuilt.

finding: The verify cannot tell its own wave from the rest of the tree — it reads git diff wholesale, so with two chats building, an overturn may belong to work the run never touched.
evidence: wf_b81e5b49-35b started with 7 src/ + 5 .claude/ files already modified.
note: Shipped with A3 on one new structured field, filesTouched per verdict, plus waveFilesNamed in the manifest. Falls back to the whole tree and SAYS so.

finding: priorClean pruning was manual — correctness depended on the Manager remembering to drop a stale 'proven clean' entry.
evidence: One entry dropped by hand during wf_b81e5b49-35b.
note: Auto-drops by basename against the wave's files, deliberately loose in the DROP direction; returns priorCleanDropped for the Manager to delete from state.verifiedClean.

finding: The 18:00 cron pinged during a long manual run, producing a spurious ask every long evening.
evidence: Correctly saw lastRun.status running and declined, so it was safe.
note: Dropped on purpose — the behaviour is correct and the only fix would suppress a message that also reports a skipped night. Moot since the cron was deleted.

finding: dependencyAsks.attached reported 0 when the machinery WORKED. The ask lives on the originator's needs-dependency row, the resume deletes that row, and the manifest counted by scanning survivors — so every ask that closed had its evidence removed before counting.
evidence: Broken in the direction that HIDES loss: the Manager's tell for lost asks is attached > routedAndBuilt + deferredToOwner, which with attached:0 can never fire.
note: Now counts asks when MINTED, via a Set of every ask id created.

finding: A malformed arg was indistinguishable from an absent one, and it cost a full dispatch.
evidence: alreadyBuilt.passedIn: 0 when 11 refs were passed. Array.isArray is false for a JSON string, and the default silently swallowed it. A lane went out in full to answer already-fixed.
note: Validate every arg at the top, attempt JSON.parse recovery on a string, warn when present-but-wrong-shaped. The manifest CAUGHT this the same night — a zero where zero was impossible.

finding: The Manager departed from the one report format, returning TWO tables with two non-spec column sets.
evidence: Owner's spec is ONE table and the charter says 'Do not improve it.'
note: Part was a real GAP: the format models BUGS but the report also carries actions and questions. Resolution: one table, fill em-dash where a column does not apply, use Status for what it split out. No new columns.

finding: OVERTURN vs DISCOVERY — the verify could trap a run in an endless cycle. A NEW problem the verifier noticed had nowhere to go, so it got smuggled into notes, read as this wave's work, and built — which invalidated the pass that found it.
evidence: Observed on row 118. Owner: 'verify should be after the pingpong end, not in the middle… now we are working for nothing.'
note: Separate discoveries array, shaped to drop straight into args.issues. An overturn belongs to this wave and blocks the wrap; a discovery is the next run's first item.

finding: Workflow({name:'…'}) serves a SESSION-CACHED copy of the engine, not the file on disk — so every edit made during a session is invisible to name-based invocation.
evidence: Confirmed against the persisted run script. A Manager chat that already invoked by name runs the pre-2026-07-27 engine: no verifier, no Sonnet lanes, none of A1-A8.
note: The Manager invokes by scriptPath always. Also retro-explains a wrong 'no mid-edit race' conclusion — a session cache looks byte-identical, so that check could never distinguish the two.

finding: args-as-a-string defeats every PER-KEY guard. The whole args OBJECT can arrive as one string, so every key reads undefined: nothing is 'present but wrong-shaped' and the engine takes the default path in silence.
evidence: That is how a described item became a 32-agent sweep costing ~2.1M tokens. A6's fix guarded the values and not the container.
note: Parse the container, then THROW on a wrong shape.

finding: bugger.js warned where it should REFUSE — asArray recovered-or-warned and continued.
evidence: A loud stop costs one re-invocation; a silent default costs a wave.
note: Shipped in the owner's shape rather than as proposed: throws only for issues (whose silent default is a full GitHub pull plus log review), warns-and-continues for everything else. Abort before the wave, never during it.

finding: The fan-out guard was a LOG, not a GATE — items.length > 8 printed a warning and swept anyway.
evidence: 32 understand agents, ~2.1M tokens, instead of planning the one item it was handed.
note: Shipped as the owner's rule, stronger than proposed: 'always do 1 unless I'M SAYING more.' Naming refs or items passes through at any count; the label-query path stops before Recon with needsChoice:true unless sweep:true.

finding: A stale SKILL copy silently changes Manager behaviour — the chat had loaded SKILL.md before a rule existed, so the rule was never in play.
evidence: Same shape as A9; neither skills nor workflow scripts announce that they cache per session.
note: Owner: 'no worries about it' — no mechanism exists, and the working habit is a fresh chat for a fresh engine. See A26, which proves the same holds for agent definitions.

finding: The Understand phase name sat wrong among noun-shaped phases (Intake, Decompose, Build, Context, Verify).
evidence: Owner's call; 'Research' rejected, 'Planner' rejected for leaking into Decompose's job.
note: Renamed Recon — vocabulary rule 9c already speaks. The internal understood arg was deliberately left at the time and renamed to recon on 2026-07-29 once nothing was in flight.

finding: Recon ran Sonnet/medium while Decompose ran Opus/xhigh, which is backwards — recon establishes the ground truth everything downstream stands on and NOTHING backstops it.
evidence: The verifier checks the diff, not whether the premise was right, and the owner cannot tell a bad code-read from a good one by reading a plan.
note: Opus/high. Verified empirically on wf_a3bfe2a3-abe: intake haiku, all 4 recon claude-opus-5.

finding: THE ENGINE'S RESULT HAS NO DURABLE HOME — persistence is the framework's most load-bearing prompt-only step, and it failed on the first wave that produced overturns.
evidence: The verify overturned four fixes; the Manager reported them as prose and wrote nothing. report.md still said 'Nothing is waiting on you' and the ledger still had all 11 rows as built, four of which were now false. Not a missing row — an actively FALSE one.
note: Root: workflow scripts have no filesystem access, so the engine physically cannot write its own result. Fix shrinks the action — a persist block with notBuilt, an assertion irreconcilable with a false report, and mustAlsoAppear counts. A copy happens more reliably than a composition.

finding: Cost claims were being estimated rather than measured, and three in one day were all wrong — each pointing at building the wrong thing.
evidence: 'Splitting a dispatch quarters the cost' (false — the per-agent floor is 70-85 turns, so splitting is WORSE); 'the guard is 45% of the day' (true of that day only); 'recon collapsed' (it had MOVED into Bash grep, where it was not counted).
note: Added to the Manager's own rules. The LANES were measuring correctly the same week; the orchestrator was the one guessing.

finding: Every standard pushes toward deletion, and NOTHING checked whether a removal took something valuable with it.
evidence: A prompt-budget cut saved ~33,500 chars and stripped Maelle's persona with the surplus. Correct code, green typecheck, no lie, no leak, met every rule — and a person had to notice. Repair cost ~1,200 chars, keeping 98% of the saving.
note: The verifier now asks the inverse question on any cut: what is gone, and did anything worth keeping go with it? Judged as harm, never as taste. The only axis where a change passes every check and still makes the product worse.

finding: Plan mode had no slot for the owner's constraints, so at plan time the ticket got a voice and he did not.
evidence: answers is declared at feature.js:61, read once at :455, consumed only in the BUILD dispatch at :474. The product chat worked round it by holding four constraints in its own context and checking recon's output for compliance afterwards.
note: A distinct constraints arg, read before phase('Recon') and threaded into the prompt. Deliberately not a reuse of answers — answers respond to openQuestions recon has not produced yet.

finding: The GitHub door hands recon a DESIGN, not an outcome. The outcome-not-implementation rule only ever reached the args.items door; intake faithfully summarises ticket bodies, which carry pre-baked designs.
evidence: All four asks on wf_a3bfe2a3-abe were implementations: gh#45 pre-decided 'No new tool', gh#51 named the file to create, gh#52 specified the columns.
note: Recon now told a ticket's design is a PROPOSAL to test against the code, never a spec to cost.

finding: The orchestrator reshaped plan pieces before the owner saw them.
evidence: Product chat's stated plan: 'Any piece that contradicts a constraint gets reshaped, not shown as-is.' But a piece contradicting a constraint is frequently recon reporting the constraint is UNACHIEVABLE — the most valuable thing that phase produces.
note: A8's 'do not suppress a discovery to keep the wave clean' in a new costume. Now: show the piece AS RETURNED, name the conflict beside it, recommend, and let him rule.

finding: The ledger cannot see that two findings are the same SHAPE. Dedupe is by rootCause file:line — right for 'is this the same bug', blind to 'is this the same invariant'.
evidence: Three rows broke ONE invariant (a model may pick a VALUE, never the TIER) and read as three unrelated findings. The product chat, reading the same rows, proposed three separate charter rules, one per lane.
note: HALF BUILT, so it stays OPEN: the --by-invariant view exists and the field is documented, but NOTHING WRITES THE TAG — it reports 308/308 untagged. Per A5 that makes it decoration until a writer sets it.

finding: The wrap clears report.md without appending the decisions it held, so every wrap resurrects decisions the owner already made.
evidence: slot-hold-release-dm-role-gate sits in --open as DECIDE while report.md had recorded 'deferred — owner: not important for now'. remaining-cached-decision-reads carries 'defer them both for tomorrow' and its date passed with nothing appended.
note: The 24-declines failure one wrap later: then the DECLINES were prose that never became rows, now the DEFERRALS are. Fix shape as A16: the wrap emits pre-formatted ledgerLines and clearing is gated on having appended them.

finding: The run manifest measures PLUMBING, not YIELD — every health field can read green while almost nothing was buildable.
evidence: wf_33541300-121: misroutedLanes 0, waveFilesNamed 1, priorCleanDropped 0, log cutoff matched the watermark exactly — while 1 of 4 findings was ever dispatchable. Owner: 'Nothing build. But have open? And have reports. Where is our clean process.'
note: No field answers 'did this run produce anything, and what stopped the rest?' Fix shape: a yield line — findings in, dispatchable, built, blocked, each with the reason. A run where 3 of 4 correctly need the owner is a GOOD run and must not look like a stalled one.

finding: A verify-raised dependency ask is deferred correctly and then scheduled NOWHERE.
evidence: A8 gave verify-raised FINDINGS a home (the discoveries array). Dependency asks got the same deferral rule and no destination. On wf_33541300-121 the verify flipped 158 to needs-dependency with a one-clause ask to instructor, and the run ended naming an incomplete fix with nothing scheduled to finish it.
note: Half of A8 was built. Fix shape: return them pre-shaped for the next run's args, exactly as discoveries already is.

finding: Agent definitions are session-cached too — the third loader, which completes the set. Engines (A9), skills (A13) and agent definitions all load once per session and none announces it.
evidence: architect.md was written with valid frontmatter and the next Agent({subagent_type:'architect'}) in the same session returned 'Agent type not found' while listing all nine pre-existing agents.
note: Two consequences: a new agent cannot be tested in the session that created it; and any session open before the tier moved onto the charters is still dispatching lanes from definitions with no model field, so they inherit the caller's model. Check with spend.cjs --day. Fix is a RULE, not code: a framework edit takes effect in a NEW session, and whoever makes one must say so.

finding: report.md's summary line is written by hand, not derived from the rows, so it can contradict the table directly beneath it
evidence: report.md:3 says '14 findings, 4 atomic, ZERO built' and 'Seven rows await you' while the table at :7 shows four rows marked built and six rows total

finding: node --check is a silent no-op on both engines, so every syntax verification of bugger.js and feature.js today reported success without parsing anything
evidence: Node v20.20.2 detects ESM syntax in a .js file and exits 0 WITHOUT parsing: identical bytes carrying a deliberate 'const x = {,}' exit 0 as .js and exit 1 as .mjs. .mjs is not the fix either — the engines use top-level return, illegal in a real module. Proven with a must-fail canary by the architect apply run; scripts/ledger-stats.cjs is .cjs so its check was real.
